payload.detail: tests/store/store.test.ts:302-318 (INV-010 over-limit test) and 400-440 (limitWorld, three BEH-028 tests) build a world with holdSeconds 1, create the customer's 5/6/4-ticket hold in tier B at T0, then call advance(2000). That hold has expiresAt T0+1000, so BEH-018/INV-007 (a held order past its expiresAt reads expired and its tickets are free) make it expired at serving time, exactly like the blocker order. The tests nonetheless assert it still counts: ticketsHeldOrPaid(c1) equals 5, 6 or 6 at lines 421, 430, 438, and the entry is dropped as over the limit at lines 315 and 419. Under the records c1 holds 0 tickets after the advance, so the entry fits the six-ticket limit (BEH-028 given is not satisfied) and is served, which is why 4 tests fail (lines 316, 420, 430, 438). Under the records the 'given' of BEH-028 (customer already holding 5 tickets) cannot be reached with the same clock instant as the blocker's expiry unless the holder's order is created later than the blocker or has a longer lifetime. I did not special-case this; the other 29 tests pass and tsc exits 0.

payload.detail: tests/app/app.test.ts:139 (check order test) moves the injected store clock forward 2h via createStore({now}) and expects 409 E_EVENT_NOT_ON_SALE from POST /orders. src/orders/index.ts createOrder (T-005, outside this task's writes) judges on-sale and expiry with Date.now() instead of the store clock, and the Store interface in design/tech.md exposes no clock accessor, so the composition root cannot supply it; the order is accepted past the sale start and the request answers 422 E_TICKET_LIMIT instead. Required change: route modules (orders, and likewise events cancel refund window and discount expiry) must read time from the store clock, or Store must expose it. All other 244 tests pass and tsc exits 0.

tests/waitlist/waitlist.test.ts:45-47 (second join by w2 with quantity 1 while the tier has available 1, after w1's first entry for quantity 2 was queued) asserts 201 with position 2. BEH-026 and CTR-014 say a tier with at least quantity tickets available answers 409 E_TICKETS_AVAILABLE; available is 1 and quantity is 1, so 1 >= 1 gives 409. The same test at lines 38-39 asserts 409 E_TICKETS_AVAILABLE for the identical state (available 1, quantity 1), and line 49-50 asserts available stays 1. The test contradicts itself and the record; no record makes a non-empty queue change the availability check. All other 237 tests pass and tsc exits 0.

payload.detail: Two frozen tests in tests/app/pipeline.test.ts contradict the records; every other test passes (260 of 262) and tsc exits 0. (1) tests/app/pipeline.test.ts:229-230 (CST-002 test) asserts POST /sessions answers 201; CTR-002 success is '200 { token }' and the sessions behaviour record says '200 with { token }'. (2) tests/app/pipeline.test.ts:209-217 (INV-011 test) posts to /orders with eventId = the cancelled event and tierId = a tier of the OTHER event, quantity 7, and expects 409 E_EVENT_NOT_ON_SALE; the tierId is not one of the cancelled event's tiers, so the input check 400 E_INVALID_TIER (CTR order endpoint, src/orders/index.ts:83) correctly decides first, and the quantity 7 would also be 422 later; the test's own fixture cannot reach the state check. Fixing either needs a test edit or a change outside the write-set (src/accounts, src/orders).

payload.detail: tests/app/app.test.ts:334 and tests/app/app.test.ts:371 assert that GET /events with no query answers { items: [], page: 1, pageSize: 20, total: 0 }. The record behind GET /events (spec/spec.md:526 and :571, implemented by T-004 in src/events and pinned by tests/events/events.test.ts:196 and :207) says the default pageSize is 10. The events module returns pageSize 10, so these two tests fail (257 of 259 pass; every other test in tests/app and tests/waitlist is green and tsc exits 0). Making them pass needs the app to inject pageSize=20, which contradicts the record, so I did not. The app tests should expect pageSize 10.
